findings.summary: tag_guard blocked a read-only tag listing, then blocked guard_note.py recording that block because the note quoted the command. One root cause: it matched the verb by regex over raw command text instead of parsing what the command DOES — the failure mode SS12 names in its own rule.
findings.disposition: Quoted text is stripped before any verb match, and creation is keyed on the FACT (a positional name, or a creation flag) rather than an allow-list of listing flags someone had to remember. Both live false positives are frozen as ALLOW rows in the guard's existing two-directional calibration table; all eleven BLOCK rows still block. Recorded through guard_note BEFORE the fix, with performed_elsewhere=yes naming the substitution, so the reroute is distinguishable from evasion.

findings.summary: The plan's stated assumption — that a subagent dispatch emits tool_name 'Task' — is FALSE. Real captures on Claude Code 2.1.234 show tool_name 'Agent'; one dispatch emits BOTH a tool_decision and a tool_result, so counting every Agent-bearing record double-counts; and no subagent_type attribute exists at all.
findings.disposition: The deliverable was evidence-gated rather than assumption-gated precisely so this could be caught: a fixture invented around 'Task' would have passed forever while production counted zero dispatches. Implemented against the verified names, counting decisions only. The per-type breakdown is NOT built — it has no supplier. Provenance is recorded in the test docstring, not merely in a commit message.

findings.summary: grade_from_otel reported telemetry-unavailable only when the TOTAL record count was zero, so an export containing ordinary tool events but no dispatch events would have printed a confident 'subagents: 0' — merging 'none happened' with 'I cannot see them'.
findings.disposition: A zero is now reported only when a tool event was actually observed, which proves the export carries tool_name; otherwise 'unmeasured'. Planted fixture: recognizable records with no tool event must yield unmeasured, never 0.

findings.summary: docs/telemetry.md's quick-capture recipe stated the console exporter writes to stderr (it writes to stdout) and implied its output is machine-readable (it is pretty-printed JS-object notation with unquoted keys; the parser recognises nothing and exits 1). The documented path had evidently never been run end-to-end.
findings.disposition: Both claims corrected, the console path marked eyeball-only, and the verified event/attribute names tabled so the next reader does not have to buy them with a live run. The parser's behaviour was correct throughout — it failed closed rather than inventing a grade.

findings.summary: The tag_guard fix is committed and tested but is NOT the guard running in live sessions: hooks execute from the installed plugin copy, which the doctor reports as 1.41.0 and older against a canonical 1.42.0. 'Fixed' here means fixed in the repo, not fixed in the session.
findings.disposition: Stated rather than rounded up, per the standing rule that committed is not deployed and deployed is not running. It was demonstrated live: after the fix passed its tests, the same read was still blocked in-session, and the doctor named the cache skew. Remains OPEN until the plugin is updated on David's machine — an action no agent can take. The doctor's PLUGIN CACHE SKEW line is the mechanical reader that will confirm it.
